questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is road safety?
questions.a: Road safety is the measures taken to prevent accidents and protect people using roads.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Who is a road user?
questions.a: A road user is any person who uses a road, such as a pedestrian, driver, passenger, cyclist, motorcyclist or animal handler.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Mention four examples of road users.
questions.a: Pedestrians, drivers, passengers and cyclists (also motorcyclists and animal handlers).

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Who is a pedestrian?
questions.a: A pedestrian is a person who walks along or crosses a road.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: State four safety rules for pedestrians.
questions.a: Any four: walk on the right side facing traffic where there is no footpath; use a footpath where provided; cross at a zebra crossing; look right, left and right again; do not run or play on the road; obey traffic lights and signs; wear bright clothing at night.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Why should pedestrians avoid playing on the road?
questions.a: Because a child playing on the road is not watching traffic and can easily be knocked down by a vehicle; roads are for vehicles, not for games.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Who is a driver?
questions.a: A driver is a person who controls and operates a vehicle.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give four safety rules for drivers.
questions.a: Any four: obey traffic rules and signs; drive at a safe speed; do not drive when drunk; do not use a mobile phone; wear a seat belt; keep the vehicle in good condition; do not overload.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Why should drivers avoid using mobile phones while driving?
questions.a: Because a mobile phone takes the driver's attention off the road and can cause an accident.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Who is a passenger?
questions.a: A passenger is a person travelling in a vehicle but not controlling it.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: State four safety rules for passengers.
questions.a: Any four: wear a seat belt; sit properly; do not distract the driver; do not put the head or hands outside; do not jump on or off a moving vehicle.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Mention four safety rules for cyclists.
questions.a: Any four: wear a properly fitted helmet; ride on the correct side; obey traffic signs; use hand signals when turning; keep the bicycle in good condition; use lights at night.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Why should motorcyclists wear helmets?
questions.a: To protect the head from injury if an accident happens.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What are road signs?
questions.a: Road signs are signs placed along roads to give information, warnings or instructions to road users.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Name the three main types of road signs.
questions.a: Warning signs, regulatory signs and information signs.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give three examples of warning signs.
questions.a: Any three: sharp bend, dangerous junction, children crossing, pedestrian crossing, road works, hump ahead, railway crossing.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give three examples of regulatory signs.
questions.a: Any three: stop, no entry, no parking, speed limit, no overtaking, give way.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give three examples of information signs.
questions.a: Any three: hospital, bus stop, parking area, telephone, petrol station.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What does a red traffic light mean?
questions.a: A red light means STOP.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What does a green traffic light mean?
questions.a: A green light means GO when the way is clear and it is safe to proceed.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Mention four causes of road accidents.
questions.a: Any four: over-speeding; driving while drunk; reckless driving; using a mobile phone while driving; overtaking in dangerous places; poorly maintained vehicles; crossing roads carelessly; overloading.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: State four effects of road accidents.
questions.a: Any four: death; injuries; disability; damage to vehicles and property; loss of income; high medical expenses; traffic congestion; emotional suffering.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give five ways of preventing road accidents.
questions.a: Any five: obeying traffic rules; avoiding over-speeding and drunk driving; wearing seat belts and helmets; maintaining vehicles; using pedestrian crossings; providing proper road signs; improving road conditions; avoiding overloading.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Why is road safety important?
questions.a: Because it prevents accidents, saves lives, reduces injuries and medical expenses, protects property and helps people use roads safely.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is a zebra crossing?
questions.a: A zebra crossing is a marked part of a road where pedestrians can cross safely.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is a debate?
questions.a: A debate is a formal discussion in which people give different opinions about a particular topic or motion.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is a motion?
questions.a: A motion is the statement or topic being debated.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Who is a proposition?
questions.a: The proposition is the side that supports the motion.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Who is an opposition speaker?
questions.a: An opposition speaker is a speaker on the side that disagrees with the motion.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Who is a chairperson?
questions.a: The chairperson is the person who controls and guides the debate.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is the work of a timekeeper?
questions.a: The timekeeper keeps track of the time given to each speaker.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Mention two types of debate.
questions.a: Formal debate and informal debate.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: State five rules of debating.
questions.a: Any five: speak clearly; respect other speakers; listen carefully; support arguments with facts and examples; avoid insulting others; follow the chairperson's instructions; keep within the time; do not interrupt.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give five qualities of a good debater.
questions.a: Any five: confident; well prepared; respectful; clear in speech; good at listening; knowledgeable; logical; persuasive; disciplined.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: How does debating help pupils?
questions.a: It helps them develop confidence, improve speaking and listening skills, develop critical thinking, express and defend opinions, respect different opinions, and improve research and leadership skills.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: How should a pupil prepare for a debate?
questions.a: Understand the motion; know your side; research the topic; identify strong arguments with examples; think about the other side's arguments; prepare answers to them; organise points logically; practise speaking clearly; keep within the time.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give four points for the motion: "Pupils should be given homework."
questions.a: Any four, for example: homework helps pupils revise what was taught in class; it builds the habit of hard work and discipline; it keeps pupils usefully busy at home; it lets parents follow the child's progress.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give four points against the motion: "Pupils should be given homework."
questions.a: Any four, for example: homework tires pupils after a long school day; it leaves little time for rest, play and home duties; some parents cannot help with the work; too much homework can make pupils dislike studying.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Why should debaters respect opposing speakers?
questions.a: Because a debate is a discussion, not a fight; respect keeps the debate orderly and makes the audience and judges take your points seriously.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is the role of the audience in a debate?
questions.a: The audience listens to the debate and may take part in the decision or voting at the end.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is a family?
questions.a: A family is a group of people related by blood, marriage or adoption who live together or care for one another.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Mention four types of families.
questions.a: Nuclear family, extended family, single-parent family and child-headed family.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is a nuclear family?
questions.a: A nuclear family consists of a father, mother and their children.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is an extended family?
questions.a: An extended family consists of parents, children and other relatives such as grandparents, uncles, aunts, nephews, nieces and cousins.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Who is a cousin?
questions.a: A cousin is a child of one's uncle or aunt.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Who is an uncle?
questions.a: An uncle is the brother of one's father or mother.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: State five importance of a family.
questions.a: Any five: it provides love and care; food and shelter; education and guidance; protection from danger; it teaches good behaviour; it gives emotional support; it helps members in difficult times; it promotes unity and cooperation; it teaches cultural values.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give five ways of promoting good family relationships.
questions.a: Any five: respecting one another; loving one another; sharing responsibilities; helping one another; communicating openly; forgiving one another; solving disagreements peacefully; caring for the elderly; spending time together; being honest.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Mention four causes of poor family relationships.
questions.a: Any four: lack of communication; poverty; domestic violence; alcohol and drug abuse; disrespect; neglect; dishonesty; quarrels; separation of parents.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: State four effects of poor family relationships.
questions.a: Any four: family conflicts; stress and unhappiness; poor academic performance; child neglect; domestic violence; separation of family members; loss of trust; school dropout.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is an occupation?
questions.a: An occupation is the work that a person does regularly to earn a living or provide a service.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give five examples of occupations.
questions.a: Any five: farming, teaching, fishing, trading, carpentry, nursing, driving, building, tailoring, banking.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is farming?
questions.a: Farming is the growing of crops and keeping of animals for food, raw materials and income.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Mention four types of farmers.
questions.a: Any four: crop farmers, poultry farmers, dairy farmers, fish farmers, pig farmers.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: State four importance of farming.
questions.a: Any four: it provides food; provides employment; provides raw materials for industries; provides income; provides goods for export; supports other businesses.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is trading?
questions.a: Trading is the buying and selling of goods and services.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Mention three examples of traders.
questions.a: Any three: shopkeepers, wholesalers, retailers, market vendors.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Who is a teacher?
questions.a: A teacher is a person who teaches — one who helps people acquire knowledge, skills and good behaviour.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Who is a carpenter?
questions.a: A carpenter is a person who does carpentry — making and repairing things mainly from wood.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Mention four products made by carpenters.
questions.a: Any four: chairs, tables, beds, doors, cupboards.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: State five factors considered when choosing an occupation.
questions.a: Any five: ability and talent; level of education; personal interests; skills; availability of employment; income expected; working conditions; availability of training; demand for the occupation; health and physical ability.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give five importance of occupations.
questions.a: Any five: they provide income; provide employment; provide goods and services; improve standards of living; promote economic development; generate government revenue; promote self-reliance; develop people's skills.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is fishing?
questions.a: Fishing is the catching or rearing of fish for food and income.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Mention three occupations related to transport.
questions.a: Any three: driver, pilot, sailor, mechanic, motorcycle rider.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Why are occupations important to a country?
questions.a: Because they provide income and employment, provide goods and services, promote economic development, generate government revenue and contribute to national development.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Name any five workers in a hotel and give the duty of each.
questions.a: Any five: waiter/waitress — serves food and drinks at table; chef — cooks the food; receptionist — receives guests and books rooms; manager — is in charge of the hotel; porter — carries guests' luggage.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give the meaning of: menu, bill, receipt, cutlery, serviette.
questions.a: Menu — the list of food and drinks with prices; bill — the paper showing how much a customer must pay; receipt — the paper showing that payment has been made; cutlery — knives, forks and spoons; serviette — the cloth or paper used to wipe the mouth and hands.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give the difference between checking in and checking out.
questions.a: Checking in is arriving at a hotel and registering for a room; checking out is leaving the hotel and paying the bill.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Name any six places found in a big hotel.
questions.a: Any six of: reception, restaurant, dining room, lounge, bar, conference room, washrooms, gym, sauna, swimming pool, kitchen, balcony.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Name the four meals mentioned in the syllabus and say when each is taken.
questions.a: Breakfast — in the morning; lunch — in the middle of the day; supper — in the evening; dinner — the main meal, usually in the evening.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is a dessert? Give three examples.
questions.a: A dessert is the sweet dish taken at the end of a meal. Examples: fruit, jelly, pudding (also ice cream, cake).

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Write a short lunch menu for a hotel, with at least five items and their prices.
questions.a: Learner's menu. It should have the hotel name and meal at the top, at least five items grouped sensibly, and a price against each.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Complete: ____ I have the bill, please?
questions.a: May

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Complete: No sooner had the guest finished eating ____ he asked for the bill.
questions.a: than

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Complete: The school ____ hold its party in the hotel conference room.
questions.a: may

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give the adjectives formed from: comfort, enjoy, beauty, expense, taste.
questions.a: comfort → comfortable; enjoy → enjoyable; beauty → beautiful; expense → expensive; taste → tasty.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Punctuate correctly: may i have the menu please said the guest
questions.a: "May I have the menu, please?" said the guest.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Write a four-line dialogue between a waiter and a customer ordering a meal.
questions.a: Learner's dialogue. It must name each speaker, start a new line for each, use quotation marks or the play format consistently, and use polite language such as May I …, please.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give any six good table manners.
questions.a: Any six of: wash hands before eating; sit upright; place the serviette on your lap; use the cutlery properly; do not talk with your mouth full; chew with your mouth closed; do not make noise with the cutlery; say please and thank you; ask to be excused before leaving the table.
accepted: place the serviette on your lap
do not talk with your mouth full
do not make noise with the cutlery
ask to be excused before leaving the table

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Write a short advertisement (about four lines) for a hotel in your town.
questions.a: Learner's advertisement. It should have the hotel name, a catchy line, the services, the price or an offer, the location and a contact.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is a dictionary? Give any four things it tells you about a word.
questions.a: A dictionary is a book that lists words in alphabetical order and gives information about them. Any four of: spelling, meaning, pronunciation, stress, part of speech, plural form, origin, example sentence.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is a thesaurus, and how is it different from a dictionary?
questions.a: A thesaurus is a book that gives words of similar meaning (synonyms) and opposites. A dictionary explains what a word means, while a thesaurus offers other words you could use instead.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Arrange in alphabetical order: orange, apple, mango, banana, pear.
questions.a: apple, banana, mango, orange, pear

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Arrange in alphabetical order: stand, stamp, state, star, stay.
questions.a: stamp, stand, star, state, stay

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Arrange in alphabetical order: chief, chair, child, chalk, cheese.
questions.a: chair, chalk, cheese, chief, child

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What are guide words?
questions.a: Guide words are the two words at the top of a dictionary page: the first word on that page and the last word on that page.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: If the guide words on a page are father — feather, which of these words are on that page: fast, feast, feed, fault?
questions.a: feast is on that page. Fast comes before father, and feed and fault fall outside the range.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What do these abbreviations stand for: n., v., adj., adv., pl.?
questions.a: n. — noun; v. — verb; adj. — adjective; adv. — adverb; pl. — plural.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Write out what this entry tells you: quick /kwɪk/ adj. fast; taking a short time.
questions.a: It tells you the spelling (quick), the pronunciation /kwɪk/, that it is an adjective, and its meaning — fast, taking a short time.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give one word for: a word formed from the first letters of other words, and give two examples.
questions.a: An acronym. Examples: UNEB, NEMA (also UWA, NGO, AIDS).

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Add question tags: A dictionary gives meanings, ____? · She isn't reading, ____? · I am late, ____?
questions.a: doesn't it? · is she? · aren't I?

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give the opposites of: cheap, arrive, polite, shallow, ancient.
questions.a: cheap → expensive; arrive → depart; polite → rude; shallow → deep; ancient → modern.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give the opposites by adding a prefix: happy, possible, legal, agree, behave.
questions.a: happy → unhappy; possible → impossible; legal → illegal; agree → disagree; behave → misbehave.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give the comparative and superlative of: tall, big, happy, expensive, good, bad.
questions.a: tall — taller — tallest; big — bigger — biggest; happy — happier — happiest; expensive — more expensive — most expensive; good — better — best; bad — worse — worst.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Complete: Peach comes ____ people in the dictionary, and people comes ____ peach.
questions.a: Peach comes before people, and people comes after peach.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give any five reasons why a dictionary is important to a P.6 learner.
questions.a: Any five of: it gives correct spellings; it explains new words; it shows pronunciation; it gives the part of speech; it improves vocabulary and composition; it settles arguments about meaning; it helps in reading and research.
accepted: it gives the part of speech
it helps in reading and research

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Which word would come first in a dictionary: market or marble? Give a reason.
questions.a: Marble, because after mar- we compare the fourth letter: b comes before k.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Use most useful correctly in a sentence.
questions.a: Learner's sentence, for example: A dictionary is the most useful book in the classroom.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Find and write any three words in this note that would appear on a dictionary page with the guide words sound — spelling.
questions.a: Any three words falling between sound and spelling alphabetically, for example sounds, speech, spell (also speaker, special).

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Write a short paragraph (about five sentences) explaining to a P.4 pupil how to look up a word in a dictionary.
questions.a: Learner's paragraph. It should tell the pupil to know the first letter of the word, open the dictionary near that letter, use the guide words at the top of the page, follow the letters one by one, and then read the meaning and the part of speech.
